set.body:
Meta-epic for a Scala 3 surface viewer over the existing renderer-free surface module. The public model, state reducer, display encoding, compiler, correctness receipts, and reference raster semantics must live in shared JVM/Scala.js code. JVM delivery is JavaFX-first: use TriangleMesh plus a dynamically updated per-face texture atlas and native PickResult, with a measured go/no-go gate before considering an LWJGL fallback. Scala.js gets a thin interactive GPU adapter compared differentially with ~/code/jscode/surfviewjs; no Three.js or JavaFX type may leak into shared APIs.

Required MVP: single and bilateral surfaces; base anatomy plus scalar, label, mask, and packed-RGBA layers; explicit visibility/order/opacity/blending/window/transparent-band semantics; lateral, medial, anterior, posterior, dorsal, and ventral views; rotate/pan/zoom/reset; exact L/R orientation policy; face/vertex picking and readouts; deterministic screenshots; cache/upload/profile receipts.

Correctness gates: validated mesh/topology identity across SurfaceSet variants; surfaceToWorld applied before camera projection; asymmetric L/R/A/P/S/I fixtures; winding, normals, culling, threshold-boundary, NaN, sparse-field, compositing-order, and picking oracles; shared reference-raster comparison; tolerant backend image comparison; affected JVM and Scala.js suites.

Performance gates: geometry upload once per mesh identity; zero geometry or texture uploads during camera-only interaction; style changes avoid geometry rebuild; timepoint/data updates touch only affected color resources; 32k and 164k vertex profiles with 1, 4, and 8 layers; p50/p95 compile, texture-update, render, and pick timings; exact bytes/uploads/draw-call receipts. Closure requires JVM and JS backend conformance, live JavaFX and browser receipts, testAll, documentation, and preservation of unrelated dirty-tree work.
set.title: Epic: cross-platform brain-surface visualization with a JavaFX-first JVM backend
